subject: Computer Networking
title: SD-WAN Appliances
description: A short lesson to help you apply SD-WAN Appliances.

hook.text: Traditional WANs use pricey MPLS circuits. SD-WAN routes over cheap internet links just as reliably.

buildup.text: SD-WAN appliances at each branch create encrypted tunnels over broadband, LTE, or any available link.

discovery.text: A central controller manages all branches. It routes video over the fastest link, backups over the cheapest.

twist.text: If one link degrades, SD-WAN switches traffic in milliseconds. No manual intervention needed.

climax.text: Companies save 60% replacing MPLS with SD-WAN. Performance often improves from multi-path routing.

punchline.text: SD-WAN makes cheap links work like expensive private ones.

quiz.question: What does an SD-WAN appliance replace?
options: Expensive MPLS circuits with software-managed internet links

details.summary: SD-WAN appliances use software-defined networking principles to manage wide area network connections, intelligently routing traffic across multiple links like MPLS, broadband, and LTE based on real-time performance.
details.whyItMatters: SD-WAN dramatically reduces WAN costs by using cheap internet links alongside or instead of expensive MPLS circuits while maintaining application performance through intelligent path selection.
takeaways: SD-WAN routes traffic across multiple WAN links intelligently
Policies steer applications to the best-performing link in real time
Central management simplifies configuration across hundreds of sites

faq.question: How does SD-WAN save money compared to MPLS?
faq.answer: MPLS circuits cost 5 to 10 times more per megabit than broadband internet. SD-WAN lets organizations use inexpensive internet links for most traffic while keeping MPLS only for latency-sensitive applications. Many organizations save 50 percent or more on WAN costs by migrating to SD-WAN.

faq.question: How does SD-WAN choose which link to use?
faq.answer: SD-WAN appliances continuously measure latency, jitter, and packet loss on each WAN link. Application-aware policies route traffic based on these measurements. Voice traffic goes to the lowest-latency link, bulk transfers use the highest-bandwidth link, and failover is automatic.
